error_types.example: [Thu Jun 09 07:11:21 2005] [error] [client 204.100.200.22] Directory index forbidden by rule: /var/www/html/
error_types.explanation: Triggered when a client requests a directory (here the document root /var/www/html/) that has no DirectoryIndex file (e.g., index.html) or where autoindexing is explicitly disabled. This is normal Apache behavior for a default Fedora/Red Hat Apache install with the Options -Indexes rule. It is NOT a security concern on its own; it just means a user typed the bare hostname/IP into their browser. The high volume simply reflects many visitors, scanners, and misconfigured clients doing so. If undesired, add an index page or enable a custom error document.

error_types.category: File does not exist - awstats CGI vulnerability scan
error_types.explanation: Automated scanners probing for the AWStats log-analyzer CGI (CVE-2005-0116, the awstats.pl 'configdir' Remote Command Execution flaw that was widely exploited in 2005). Requests target paths like /cgi, /awstats, /awstats.pl, /awstats/awstats.pl, and /stats/awstats.pl. SECURITY CONCERN: this is hostile reconnaissance/exploitation traffic. Even though the target is an IIS/Apache-CGI box, every probe should be treated as an attempted compromise. Recommended actions: install mod_security rules for the awstats exploit signature, block/alert on the source IPs, and ensure awstats (if installed at all) is patched.

error_types.category: File does not exist - Nimda/Code Red IIS worm probes
error_types.explanation: Classic Nimda/Code Red worm signatures: scanners hit a long list of IIS-only paths (scripts/root.exe, MSADC, _vti_bin, _mem_bin, msadc, /c, /d, and Unicode/double-decoded traversal strings like /scripts/..%5c.., /scripts/..\xc1\x1c.., /scripts/..\xc0\xaf.., /scripts/..\xc1\x9c.., /scripts/..%2f.., /scripts/..%5c%5c..). This server is Apache/Linux, so all probes return 404, but the traffic is hostile. SECURITY CONCERN: yes - these are infected hosts attempting to spread. Monitor source IPs, consider fail2ban/iptables rate-limiting on 404s, and ensure mod_security is enabled (it is: mod_security/1.9dev2 is loaded).

mod_jk2 failed to initialise a child worker process. The trailing number is the return code from the JNI bridge: '1 0' means the parent registered a worker but a code path returned 0 (non-fatal), while '1 -2' means the child could not find its slot in the shared scoreboard (see the paired jk2_init() 'Can't find child' errors). This is a SERVER-INTERNAL misconfiguration of the Tomcat/Apache jk2 connector (workers2.properties / scoreboard shared memory). It is not a client security concern, but it indicates broken JSP/servlet routing and warrants upgrading from the deprecated mod_jk2 to mod_jk 1.2.x or mod_proxy_ajp.

error_types.category: jk2_init() Can't find child in scoreboard
error_types.example: [Thu Jun 09 19:23:32 2005] [error] jk2_init() Can't find child 4057 in scoreboard
error_types.explanation: The mod_jk2 connector looks up Apache child PIDs in its shared-memory scoreboard (configured in workers2.properties) and cannot locate them - usually because the scoreboard file/socket permissions, the JNI socket, or the JVM worker pool is misconfigured. SERVER-INTERNAL: not a security issue, but it means Tomcat-backed URLs will fail with 500s until mod_jk is fixed. Recommend migrating off the long-obsolete mod_jk2 (which was removed from Apache 2.2+ entirely).

Mass 'sumthin' scanner: tools that sweep huge IP ranges requesting /sumthin, /scripts/sumthin.htm or similar probe strings, looking for misconfigured IIS servers that auto-execute anything in the scripts/ directory. SECURITY CONCERN: this is automated worm/scan traffic. The bursts (47 hits from one IP in a few seconds) confirm scripted scanning. Mitigation is the same as for other scanner categories - mod_security rules, rate-limiting, and IP blocking.

error_types.example: [Sat Jun 11 03:03:03 2005] [error] [client 202.133.98.6] script not found or unable to stat: /var/www/cgi-bin/awstats
error_types.explanation: Same AWStats exploit scanners as rank 2, but this time the requests land on the cgi-bin path (/cgi-bin/awstats and /cgi-bin/awstats.pl) so Apache logs 'script not found or unable to stat' instead of 'File does not exist'. SERVER-INTERNAL note: the script truly isn't installed, which is good - the attempts are harmless 404s. SECURITY CONCERN: yes, hostile exploitation traffic targeting CVE-2005-0116; monitor and block source IPs.

error_types.category: File does not exist - generic _vti_bin probe
error_types.explanation: Standalone probes of the FrontPage Server Extensions / SharePoint path /_vti_bin. Some are Nimda-related (rank 3), but this category captures _vti_bin hits that appear outside the full Nimda sequence - often Nimda variant worms, FrontPage-exploit bots, or SharePoint discovery scans. SECURITY CONCERN: yes, hostile reconnaissance. Same mitigations as the other scanner categories.

error_types.example: [Sat Jun 11 03:03:08 2005] [error] [client 202.133.98.6] script not found or unable to stat: /var/www/cgi-bin/stats
error_types.explanation: AWStats scanner looking for a /cgi-bin/stats wrapper (AWStats is sometimes installed under that name). SERVER-INTERNAL: harmless 404 since the script does not exist. SECURITY CONCERN: same as the other awstats categories - this is exploit traffic for CVE-2005-0116.

error_types.example: [Sat Jun 11 14:32:51 2005] [error] [client 212.238.198.203] script not found or unable to stat: /var/www/cgi-bin/openwebmail
error_types.explanation: Scanner looking for the OpenWebMail Perl CGI, which had multiple historical command-execution vulnerabilities (e.g., CVE-2003-0285 and the 2005 file-upload bypass). 20 rapid-fire requests from one IP indicate an automated scanner. SECURITY CONCERN: yes, hostile reconnaissance for known OpenWebMail flaws. If OpenWebMail is genuinely not installed (the 404s imply so), the probes fail safely; still recommend blocking the source IP.

error_types.category: Invalid HTTP method (cmd.exe / Unicode path-traversal exploit)
error_types.example: [Fri Jun 10 01:23:50 2005] [error] [client 63.203.254.140] Invalid method in request get /scripts/.%252e/.%252e/winnt/system32/cmd.exe?/c+dir
error_types.explanation: Apache rejects these because the request line begins with a lowercase 'get' (the HTTP method is case-sensitive and must be 'GET') and/or contains the URL-decoded cmd.exe path-traversal string (Unicode %c0%af, %e0%80%af, double-encoded %252e, %35c, %5c, %c1%9c, etc.). These are Nimda/Code Red variants and IIS unicode-exploit scanners (IIS CVE-2000-0884, Nimda). SECURITY CONCERN: yes, this is direct exploitation traffic. Apache rejects it before the path is even resolved, so the host is safe, but the source IPs are infected and should be monitored.

error_types.example: [Thu Jun 09 06:07:05 2005] [error] env.createBean2(): Factory error creating channel.jni:jni ( channel.jni, jni)
error_types.explanation: SERVER-INTERNAL error from mod_jk2's JNI layer at startup: the config object (channel.jni:jni, vm:, worker.jni:onStartup, worker.jni:onShutdown) cannot be instantiated because the in-process JVM/JNI bridge is unavailable - typically because no JDK is installed for httpd, JNI is disabled, or workers2.properties points to a non-existent JVM. Not a security concern, but it breaks all Tomcat integration. Appears in pairs (4 factory errors + 4 config.update errors per restart) and recurs on every Apache restart.

Follow-on SERVER-INTERNAL error from mod_jk2 emitted immediately after each createBean2() failure: the config-update pass cannot register the failed JNI object. Root cause and remediation are identical to rank 12 (install/configure the JVM for mod_jk2, or better, migrate to mod_jk 1.2.x or mod_proxy_ajp). Not a security issue.

error_types.category: File does not exist - other miscellaneous paths
error_types.explanation: Residual 404s that fall outside the other scanner patterns - mostly collateral from the awstats scanner (e.g., /cgi, /awstats.pl, /stats/awstats.pl) plus a handful of stray requests. Many of these are still attack-related reconnaissance, but the category is intentionally the 'catch-all' for File-does-not-exist entries. SECURITY CONCERN: low to moderate; mostly harmless 404s, but the source IPs should be tracked.

error_types.example: [Sun Jun 12 05:05:35 2005] [error] [client 210.91.137.35] request failed: URI too long (longer than 8190)
error_types.explanation: Apache's default LimitRequestLine (8190 bytes) was exceeded - the client sent an URL longer than ~8 KB. Often a symptom of buffer-overflow probes or buggy clients (e.g., a worm stuffing long Unicode traversal strings into the request line, or a broken WebDAV/FrontPage client). SECURITY CONCERN: low - Apache rejects the request before any processing, but a sudden spike of these from one IP is a strong indicator of probing/exploitation attempts and should be investigated.
